title: Dedicated capacity SLA onboarding heuristic and GPU-fallback ladder
creator: Anika Desai
description: Goal: Create a deterministic, operator-friendly intake heuristic that maps enterprise reserved capacity requests to an initial SLA band, recommended reserved throughput, GPU class, and an automated fallback ladder. Scope: non-bug dedicated capacity intake (new enterprise customers or major workload changes). Deliverables: 1) a one-page heuristic for intake calls; 2) a decision table mapping workload fingerprints to GPU class recommendations; 3) a GPU-fallback ladder and burst policy for each SLA band; 4) required data fields for the intake form; 5) a small set of templated canary + rollback policies for onboarding. Constraints: we must avoid requiring customers to provide detailed token-level profiling during initial intake; recommendations should be conservative and gracefully degrade costs. Success metrics: reduce back-and-forth intake cycles by 50%, decrease onboarding time from handoff to first accepted reservation by 40%, and surface clear SLO targets in the contract. This ticket coordinates PM, Solutions, SRE, and Eng for design and initial implementation of the heuristic.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page intake heuristic doc (Confluence) that CX and AE can follow without deep infra knowledge
Decision table that outputs: SLA Band (Gold/Silver/Bronze), reserved throughput (tokens/sec or RPS), initial GPU class recommendation, and fallback ladder
A minimal required intake form (6 fields) plus examples filled for three canonical workloads (query, chat, batching)
Implementation plan for adding heuristic output into the onboarding playbook and Console intake checklist
Sign-off from SRE and Eng on fallback ladder and burst policy (documented in GitHub RFC link)

decisions: SLA bands: Gold (99.9% availability, p95 latency target documented), Silver (99% availability), Bronze (best-effort reservation)
GPU ladder by default: Gold -> H100; Silver -> A100; Bronze -> L4; explicit override allowed for cost-constrained customers with engineering review
Reserved throughput units will be expressed as tokens/sec for generation workloads and qps for fixed-payload embedding endpoints
Burst policy: Gold gets pre-warmed burst credits (2x reserved throughput for 5 minutes), Silver gets 1.5x for 2 minutes, Bronze none
Autoscaling policy for reserved pools: prefer vertical scaling (GPU class fallback) over immediate horizontal scale-up when latency SLO is violated, to limit cross-tenant jitter
tradeoffs_and_risks: Conservative initial recommendations reduce failed onboards but increase cost for customers who could have used smaller GPUs after profiling
Fallback ladder that prefers lower-latency GPUs first risks capacity exhaustion in rare peak windows — requires burst-credit governance
Expressing throughput as tokens/sec is unfamiliar to some sales reps; requires clear conversion guidance and examples
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Publish heuristic and intake form to AE and Solutions (2 weeks). Phase 2: Add Console guidance that surfaces the recommended SLA band and GPU class during intake (engineering spike + 1 sprint). Phase 3: Pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers, collect telemetry, and iterate the decision table. Full rollout contingent on pilot success and SRE sign-off.
